ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 11-14 and 50, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (mandatory beneficial ownership notification to CIPC); Companies Regulations 2011; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); FIC Directive 3 (2023) and FIC Guidance Notes 6A/6B (PEP related).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (non-public register: accessible to CIPC, FIC, SARS, Department of Home Affairs, and accountable institutions conducting FICA due diligence; no public or nominee-hostile disclosure)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of residence (e.g., Chinese notary for China-domiciled UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state (China is an Apostille Convention party since 7 November 2023); no consular legalization required between Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider; certification by notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of origin state; if the document is South African-issued, apostille by DIRCO after notarial certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorising local incorporation and statutory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African notary public (for foreign principals: notarised in origin state and apostilled)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route; consular legalization would be required only where the origin state is not a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certified extract from the foreign company register for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation extract for a Chinese corporate investor)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in origin state, followed by apostille; certified English or South African official-language translation attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed fit-and-proper declarations and consent-to-act declarations of proposed directors (CIPC forms)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed directors before a Commissioner of Oaths or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Commissioner of Oaths signature within South Africa; foreign-signed forms must be notarised and apostilled in the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions, and South African designations under POCDATARA. PEP status assessed under FIC Guidance Notes 6A/6B, including domestic PEP cooling-off periods of 5 years from date of ceasing office. Any positive hit or PEP classification triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and, where required, filing of a suspicious transaction report under section 29 of FICA. Screening must be repeated at onboarding and at least quarterly thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) e-Services transactional portal — https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must consist of ordinary words in one of South Africa's 11 official languages or in a recognised foreign language with a certified transliteration into English or Afrikaans. The name must end with the mandatory corporate indicator '(Pty) Ltd' or 'Proprietary Limited' (section 11(2)(a) read with Companies Regulation 15). The name must not be offensive, misleading, or imply a connection to the state, a regulator, a university, or an embassy (section 11(3)); foreign-language names require a notarised translation for CIPC examination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government, Parliament, Reserve Bank, Republic, National, State (requires ministerial or Director-General consent)
Bank, Building Society, Trust, Insurance, Financial Services (FSCA approval reserved under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 and related statutes)
University, College, Academy, School, Institute (Department of Higher Education and Training consent; relevant where study-abroad placement services are advertised)
Consulate, Embassy, Ambassador, Diplomat, Mission (irrebuttably misleading)
Audit, Chartered, Certified (requires professional body consent and is generally unavailable to a generic consulting entity)
Names substantially identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or trademark (section 12(1) objection ground)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reservation window of 60 days under Companies Regulation 13(2) cannot be extended; if the incorporation is not completed within that period, a fresh name reservation must be filed. On rejection, the applicant may immediately file a corrected alternative name reservation via CIPC eServices without prejudice. If the rejection is based on section 11(3), the applicant may lodge written representations with the CIPC Director of Company and Intellectual Property within 20 business days of the rejection notice. A final administrative appeal lies to the Companies Tribunal under section 4(4) of the Companies Act read with Companies Regulations 145-153, which must be lodged within 30 days of the final CIPC refusal. Thereafter, judicial review is available in the High Court on grounds under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance. Section 23(3)(b) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requires a physical registered address in South Africa at which legal process and regulatory notices may be served. A mail-forwarding or PO-Box-only virtual office is non-compliant for an accountable institution under FICA. A serviced office with a dedicated desk, signage, and on-site access to statutory records satisfies CIPC and FIC supervisory expectations for this advisory industry. A purely remote or virtual address without physical presence is assessed as insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Conservatively 50% during the first two compliance years. CIPC compliance monitoring, SARS, and FIC risk-based supervision may conduct unannounced on-site inspections of a registered office. An immigration and visa advisory company that processes escrow funds and wire transfers is treated as a medium-high-risk enforcement focus, particularly in the post-FATF enhanced follow-up context; statutory records, client files, and AML/CFT documentation must be immediately available at the physical address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), ss. 11 (name), 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration), 19 (legal personality), 33 (company records), 34 (share capital), 40 (consideration for shares), 66 (board); Companies Regulations, 2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic), utilising the e-Services (BizPortal) filing system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI); the company is registered only upon CIPC issue of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a (Pty) Ltd under ss. 34 and 40 of the Companies Act; shares may be issued for any consideration approved by the board. Client monies received for study-abroad and immigration visa services must be segregated in a dedicated escrow/client trust account and may not be used as operating working capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 having been completed, the Memorandum of Incorporation is adopted and ratified; (2) that the initial subscriber shares are allotted and issued, and share certificates shall be signed and delivered to each allottee; (3) that the registered office is approved at the physical address recorded with CIPC; (4) that the individuals named in the consent forms are appointed as first directors, and a Managing Director is appointed to act singly; (5) that the Managing Director and directors are authorised to open bank and escrow accounts and to file tax and licensing registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — e-Services portal (BizPortal) under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC e-Services using an authorised profile or a registered CIPC agent. Complete and submit Form CoR 9.1 naming up to three preferred names in priority order and verify that each proposed name is not offensive, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name under s. 11(2) of the Companies Act. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee electronically and retain the transaction reference and acknowledgement number for use in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 — Application for Reservation of Name
Certified copies of directors'/incorporators' South African IDs or foreign passports
Proof of payment of the CIPC name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused pursuant to s. 11, file an amended CoR 9.1 with alternative name choices. If a third party lodges an objection, respond in writing to CIPC within 20 business days; an adverse CIPC decision may be appealed to the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum of Incorporation and Incorporation Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and the appointed CIPC registered agent (internal preparatory step preceding the public filing).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI) for a proprietary limited company, specifying the share categories, any permissible exclusions or alterations to the default Companies Act provisions, and identifying the first directors. Each incorporator must sign the MoI and complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation). Confirm that the name reservation reference is quoted and that the proposed registered office will be a physical address in South Africa rather than a post office box.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI) signed by all incorporators
Form CoR 14.1 — Notice of Incorporation
CIPC name reservation reference number
Signed consent to act as director from each proposed first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MoI is queried for invalid share provisions, non-compliant governance clauses, or missing incorporator signatures, revise the affected clauses to conform with s. 15 of the Companies Act and the Companies Regulations, and re-execute the instrument before resubmission without an additional state assessment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Notice of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — e-Services / BizPortal (Companies Register).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the CIPC e-Services company registration module and upload the completed and signed CoR 14.1 together with the signed MoI. Confirm the statutory incorporation fee and effect payment. Upon verification, CIPC registers the company and issues the Certificate of Incorporation together with the assigned company registration number. The company acquires legal personality on the date of registration in terms of s. 19 of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form CoR 14.1
Final signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI)
Proof of payment of the statutory incorporation fee
Approved name reservation reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the filing for an unpaid fee, defective MoI, or name mismatch, cure the defect within the notified correction period (generally 20 business days) and resubmit. If registration is refused altogether, file a fresh application or appeal the decision to the Companies Tribunal within 60 days, retaining all CIPC correspondence as evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Statutory Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the incorporated (Pty) Ltd (internal corporate governance; notifications to CIPC where required by ss. 36 and 70).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting and pass a written resolution adopting: (a) the allotment and issue of the initial subscriber shares; (b) the registered office physical address; (c) the appointment of the first directors and the Managing Director; (d) the bank mandates and escrow account signatories; and (e) the record-keeping registers and minute book. File any prescribed notice of director or registered office particulars with CIPC within the statutory timelines.
required_dossiers: Signed Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
Register of directors and prescribed officer particulars
Registered office address confirmation
Bank mandate and escrow signatory forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an anomaly in the resolutions, minutes, or director appointments is discovered, ratify the action by a subsequent written board resolution signed by all directors and, where applicable, file correcting notices with CIPC using the appropriate prescribed form (such as CoR 27 for change of registered office) before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Employer and Compliance Registration with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling (income tax, PAYE, UIF, SDL and VAT registration).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a SARS eFiling taxpayer profile for the company and register for income tax. Register for VAT where taxable turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed the R1 million threshold. Register as an employer for PAYE, Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Skills Development Levy (SDL) via the relevant EMP10x registration form. Obtain the income tax reference number, employer registration number, and tax clearance status; note that SARS receives incorporation data electronically from CIPC, so the eFiling profile must be activated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
First board resolution authorising tax registration
Certified identity documents of directors
Registered office and business address details
Company bank account particulars for refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS fails to issue the tax reference number or queries the employer or VAT registrations, submit a corrected registration application electronically or attend a SARS branch with original identity documents; respond to any SARS notice within the stated deadline and retain the eFiling acknowledgement slips as proof of compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Licensing — Private Employment Agency Registration and Immigration Recognition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) — Employment Services Branch; Department of Home Affairs (DHA) — Immigration Services; Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) for investment-linked advisory conduct.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the provincial DEL labour centre for registration as a private employment agency under the Employment Services Act 4 of 2014. Obtain any applicable DHA recognition or authorisation to render immigration and visa representation services under the Immigration Act 13 of 2002. Open and maintain a segregated client trust/escrow account for study-abroad and visa deposits, ensuring FSCA and Consumer Protection Act disclosure and conduct standards are observed. Commence commercial advertising only after the relevant certificates have been issued.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
SARS tax clearance certificate
Signed company resolution and Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' declarations and police clearance certificates
Proof of registered office premises
Client escrow account confirmation letter from the bank
Private employment agency application form and DHA representation authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DEL or DHA application is refused or queried, remedy the stated defects (such as outstanding documentation or premises clearance) within the administrative cure period and resubmit; pursue the statutory appeal or internal review mechanism provided by the Employment Services Act or the Immigration Act, and maintain a complete correspondence file to support annual renewal and good-standing evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) — Employment Services Branch; Department of Home Affairs (DHA) — Immigration Services; Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) where the golden visa advisory involves investment-linked products.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Registration Certificate (Employment Services Act 4 of 2014); Immigration Practitioner / Visa Representation Recognition (Immigration Act 13 of 2002); Category I Financial Services Provider licence under FAIS Act 37 of 2002 if investment-linked residency advice is rendered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) — Environmental Authorisation Branch, together with the applicable municipal environmental health department.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Listing Notice 1 Category administrative office-based consultancy activity; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required, but a Basic Assessment would be triggered only if the company later establishes a training campus, student accommodation, or other built facility requiring environmental authorisation under NEM: A Act 107 of 1998.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office premises must comply with municipal sewerage and wastewater discharge bylaws; volatile organic compound and particulate emissions are negligible for a consultancy; electronic waste and confidential client-file destruction must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 and the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013; ventilation and workplace air standards under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certificate and Certificate of Occupancy in accordance with the National Building Regulations and the Fire Brigade Services Act; electrical certificate of compliance issued by an approved inspector; general duties and occupational health clearance for office workers under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; no heavy machinery or hazardous substances are present in the consultancy operating model.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 bill of entry)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing removal from South Africa
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (Authorised Dealer BOP record)
Original commercial/tax invoice and signed contract
VAT 264 export refund schedule (if refund claimed) and vendor's VAT 201 return
Non-resident status evidence and service performance records for zero-rated exported services

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, with delegated exchange-control administration granted to Authorised Dealers, being the domestic commercial banks licensed by SARB in terms of the Banks Act, 1990.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is a free-floating currency and is fully convertible for current-account transactions. A (Pty) Ltd engaged in international student placement and immigration advisory may receive and disburse current-account payments freely through an Authorised Dealer without prior FinSurv approval, provided each transaction is accompanied by complete FICA/KYC documentation, correct SARB Balance of Payments (BOP/EDI) purpose codes, and appropriate supporting invoices. Capital-account transactions remain restricted: inward non-resident equity investment above prescribed thresholds, offshore shareholder loans, and any 'loop-structure' or hybrid debt/equity arrangements require FinSurv approval; those below thresholds may proceed through the AD with a post-arrival declaration within the statutory period. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted without FinSurv approval once the original investment has been declared to the AD, but practical hurdles remain: payment of the 20% Dividends Tax (or reduced treaty rate under an applicable double-taxation agreement), satisfaction of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 solvency-and-liquidity test, audited or reviewed financial statements supporting the dividend, a board resolution with dividend declaration, and a complete SARB dividend remittance form plus favourable SARS tax-compliance status where the bank requires it.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the entity as an exporter of services, all foreign-currency proceeds derived from advisory visa and student-placement services rendered to non-residents must be repatriated to South Africa and surrendered to an Authorised Dealer within 180 days of the invoice date or the date of service completion. There is no mandatory percentage conversion into rand: the exporter may convert the full proceeds into ZAR or retain them in a foreign-currency account (FCA) held with the Authorised Dealer. The AD must receive the commercial invoice, evidence of service delivery, the SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation, and the prescribed export/rendering declaration. Proceeds may not be retained in an offshore bank account without prior FinSurv approval, and late repatriation attracts exchange-control penalties and may trigger the AD's enhanced due-diligence review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (ZAR and Multi-Currency FCA)
Operational Account with dedicated Trust/Fiduciary Receivables mechanism
Operational Account and Corporate Trust/Security Account
High-touch Operational Account and Private Client Escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW as a primary operating treasury. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud) do not hold a South African banking licence and are not Authorised Dealers under Exchange Control Regulation 10; they cannot provide a ZAR-clearable, FICA-compliant corporate account with an SA clearing number, and routing client funds through such providers to bypass the domestic AD network would constitute an exchange-control contravention. Feasibility: MEDIUM only in an ancillary collection-aggregator function where the EMI maintains a formal correspondent partnership with a licensed South African AD and all funds ultimately settle into the entity's SA bank account with a complete audit trail and per-transaction tagging; the entity must disclose the arrangement to its SA bank during onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001) permits non-face-to-face onboarding where the bank applies reliable, independent electronic verification technology, and there is no absolute statutory mandate requiring physical appearance. In practice, the major SA banks require a physical in-branch interview for the principal director, beneficial owner(s), and operative signatories where the shareholder is non-resident, the company is newly incorporated, or the sector carries Medium-Risk Enhanced exposure as in cross-border advisory. The practical accepted protocol is hybrid: apostilled or notarised CIPC corporate extracts, certified identification and proof-of-residential-address for every director and beneficial owner, a live video-call KYC interview for non-resident directors, and final in-branch signature verification by the resident authorised representative or an attorney acting as an accountable institution/mandated intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments from a student's parents, relatives, or corporate sponsors located in a different jurisdiction than the contractual student, creating a layering red flag in tuition and visa-fee collection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client engagement agreement and itemised tuition-fee invoice; notarised sponsor affidavit confirming the third-party relationship; proof of family bond or sponsorship mandate (birth/marriage certificate, corporate resolution); source-of-funds packet for each remitter comprising three months of bank statements, salary slips or audited corporate financials, and tax documents; FICA-compliant identity verification of the payer; and a payment-to-invoice reconciliation ledger evidencing no overpayment, split-payment, or refund mismatch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire transfers originating from high-risk, partially sanctioned, or high-corruption-risk source markets frequently associated with student-migrant corridors (certain African, Middle Eastern, and CIS jurisdictions), where immigration products may attract proceeds of corruption or financial crime.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time institutional sanctions screening against UN, OFAC, UK, and EU sanctions lists; a documented jurisdiction-risk rating matrix applied at onboarding; enhanced due diligence (EDD) on the remitter and ultimate beneficial owner with STR/CBTR threshold monitoring; SWIFT MT103 trail with correct BOP purpose codes; board-level AML sign-off embedded in the institution's FICA risk-management programme; and an automated refusal-and-escalation log for any sanctioned or negative-media counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-departure client funds held in a single corporate bank account may be construed as unregistered deposit-taking or unregulated client-money custody where the immigration/education placement licence is not evidenced or the funds are commingled with operating cash.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal escrow or controlled-money agreement governed by South African law; strict segregation of client funds from working capital in a dedicated account; a maintained Client Funds Register and monthly reconciliation; use of the bank's licensed fiduciary, trust, or client-money product or a South African attorney's trust account; the applicable immigration/study-agency statutory licence issued by the responsible regulator; and disclosure of the exact legal basis for holding the funds to the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A beneficial owner, director, or client applicant is identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), which is common in investor-migration and golden-visa programmes and mandatorily triggers enhanced due diligence and likely compliance escalation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening performed at onboarding and maintained through daily transaction monitoring; independent source-of-wealth opinion from a South African attorney or licensed financial adviser; SARS tax-compliance status for the entity and, where relevant, the client; complete source-of-funds documentation (notarised sale agreements, inheritance instruments, tax assessments, and audited financials); written PEP rationale filed in the FICA risk-management programme; and ongoing monitoring records confirming that all transactional flows remain consistent with the declared purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy among the entity's CIPC registered address, SARS income-tax and VAT registrations, and the physically operated office, producing a shell-company impression and risking onboarding refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date CIPC extracts reflecting the exact legal structure; street-level documented operational address with a utility bill or rental lease in the entity's name; SARS income-tax and VAT registration numbers with Letters of Good Standing; local business licences for immigration and study-advisory services; an entity-own office or co-working services agreement; and, if requested, the prior-year reviewed financial statements demonstrating operational substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection: SWIFT MT103/MT202 routed to the South African Authorised Dealer with BOP purpose code 4011 (direct investment in equity capital) and the narrative 'share subscription'; the AD issues an inward-transfer notification and the company files the prescribed Foreign Investment Declaration/EDI return with FinSurv within the statutory timeframe. Shareholder loans: SWIFT MT103 with BOP purpose code 4012 (direct investment in loan capital), supported by a formal shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length terms, a fixed or floating rate, and an express non-conversion undertaking; FinSurv prior approval is required where prescribed thresholds are exceeded or the debt structure carries hybrid features. Client funds for study-abroad and immigration services: must be directed to a separate client-escrow or segmented receivables account using the SARB service-sector BOP category applicable to business advisory services, with each wire reflecting a unique client reference; advance client funds may not be treated as operational liquidity before service performance, and all receipts must be reconciled to signed fee agreements to avoid any inference of unlawful deposit-taking.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for university tuition, visa-authority fees, government immigration levies, and overseas partner commissions; the narrative field must quote the invoice number, a precise purpose description, and the student's unique identifier to prevent beneficiary-bank holds and AML referral. Where the beneficiary bank requires correspondent intermediation, SWIFT MT202 COV with cover is used to segregate instruction from funds. Bank-issued commercial documentary credits are not economically relevant to a service placement model, but irrevocable payment undertakings to a foreign university may be structured as a direct AD instruction with an accompanying FEC. Domestic disbursements to sub-agents and immigration consultants should settle through the South African local clearing system (ACB/Samisoft) and remain tagged by file reference, invoice, and beneficiary identity. A licensed payment-service provider may aggregate low-value disbursements only where the provider is an accountable institution registered with the Financial Intelligence Centre and every underlying transaction remains separately reconstructable by the treasury function.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) concluded with a South African Authorised Dealer strictly against documented current-account exposure (for example, a contracted and dated tuition-fee liability in USD, GBP, EUR, or AUD); maturities must match the underlying receivable or payable and rollovers require a valid underlying exposure.

Structured flexible-forward arrangements offered by the AD in respect of the entity's service invoices and escrow liabilities where the amounts are reasonably determinable and evidencing a firm commercial commitment.

Onshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not available: South African corporate hedgers are restricted to deliverable onshore FECs quoted against the rand; NDF pricing may be accessed only through an approved offshore treasury conduit, which is ordinarily not granted to a domestic service consultancy.

Currency options (vanilla foreign-currency put/call options) and zero-cost collars written by the South African AD on a back-to-back basis are permissible for bona fide transactional exposures, subject to the bank's derivatives suitability assessment under FAIS and the company's internal treasury policy; speculative premium-only or vega-focused option strategies are prohibited.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) are permissible only with prior FinSurv approval and only where the treasury holds a genuine term balance-sheet exposure, such as a long-dated shareholder loan funding the operational footprint; outright speculation through swaps is not permitted.

Natural hedging via multi-currency Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs) and Foreign Currency Borrowings (FCBs) maintained at the AD enables the entity to match USD, EUR, GBP, and AUD fee inflows against overseas university and partner disbursements, reducing derivative dependency; overnight FCA positions remain subject to SARB position-limits as determined by each Authorised Dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (AR) to CIPC including the Beneficial Ownership confirmation schedule on Form CoR 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the date of incorporation; filing must be lodged within 30 business days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late penalty of ZAR 500 (approx. USD 27) per annum; failure to file within 90 days after the anniversary triggers a CIPC compliance notice and deregistration investigation; persistent non-filing results in administrative strike-off and personal liability of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) with annual financial statements or supporting schedules submitted to SARS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the company's financial year-end (annual assessment cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly administrative penalty of up to 10% of the assessed amount; SARS estimated assessment and prescribed-rate interest; criminal prosecution for repeated non-filing; suspension of tax clearance certificate blocking immigration license renewal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual PAYE Reconciliation (EMP501) for employees, if any, with interim and current declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 May of each year for the tax year ending the preceding 28 February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS penalty of up to 10% per month of under-declared or undistributed PAYE; failure to reconcile blocks the CSD tax compliance certificate and incurs additional interest and penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) filing with CIPC (conditional; required where the company's public interest score is 350 or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after board approval of the AFS and in all cases within 6 months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compliance notice with administrative penalty; continued failure constitutes an offence under the Companies Act, 2008, leading to director prosecution and company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Risk and Compliance Return (RCR) under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001, reflecting AML/CTF controls for the study-abroad and visa fee escrow payment rails
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the institution's annual reporting period (financial year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to ZAR 10 million (approx. USD 546,000) for accountable institutions; compliance notices, per-day penalties, and referral of serious contraventions to the National Prosecuting Authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit arises where the Public Interest Score (PIS) computed under Regulation 26 of the Companies Act, 2008 is (i) at least 500; (ii) at least 350 where the annual financial statements were compiled internally by the company rather than by an independent accounting professional; or (iii) the company operates client escrow payment rails as an accountable institution under the FIC Act and the relevant supervisory body requires audited financial statements. An independent review, not a full audit, is required for PIS of 100–349, or PIS of 350–499 with externally compiled AFS; no audit or independent review applies for PIS below 100.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs as approved by the Accounting Standards Board of South Africa; South Africa has no separate Local GAAP, and the annual financial statements must be prepared on the accrual basis in South African rand.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) and annually confirm its contents to CIPC as part of the Annual Return filing; any transfer of issued shares or change of beneficial interest must be lodged with CIPC on Form CoR 44.1 within 30 days of the transaction, and the BOR must be reconciled each year before the annual return is filed. The BOR, together with share transfer records, must be available for inspection by CIPC, SARS, the FIC, and the relevant immigration licensing authority.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Ownership (Form CoR 44.1 filings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 160 – 650 per annum (ZAR 3,000 – 12,000) for a CIPC-accredited registered office and company secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,600 – 4,300 per annum (ZAR 30,000 – 80,000) for an SME statutory audit or independent review by a registered audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate income tax rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for earlier years. A qualifying Small Business Corporation under section 12E is taxed on a graduated scale with an effective 0% to 21% low-income bracket and a 27% marginal rate above the upper threshold.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Africa does not grant general tax holidays. Effective tax-rate reducers include the section 11D research-and-development allowance (up to 150% deduction on approved qualifying expenditure), section 12B renewable-energy allowances, section 12C plant-and-machinery wear-and-tear allowances, section 12H learnership allowances, urban-development zone deductions and the Employment Tax Incentive for eligible youth employees. An international student placement and immigration visa advisory business generally earns ordinary trading income not eligible for sector-specific tax holidays.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry; assessed losses may be carried forward indefinitely for set-off against future taxable income, subject to the section 20A continuity-of-trade and change-in-ownership restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 Corporate Income Tax Return; mandatory electronic filing via the South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the entity's year of assessment, which for a company is normally its financial year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months of the financial year-end unless SARS stipulates a different deadline on the return. SARS will generate a filing deadline on the eFiling profile and may dispatch a reminder before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Entity particulars and SARS income tax reference number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, company registration number, income tax reference number, registered office, principal place of business, financial year start and end, number of directors and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the South African company or permanent establishment identifier. If foreign-owned, disclose the ultimate foreign parent, country of residence and any South African branch relationship.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All receipts or accruals from the business, excluding VAT and amounts of a capital nature. For the ISIC 7810 business this includes student placement fees, visa advisory fees, immigration consultant charges, agency commissions, escrow services fees and any other revenue recognised under the accrual rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident company is taxed on worldwide income. A non-resident with a South African permanent establishment must include only South African-source gross income attributable to that permanent establishment, correctly applying the relevant double taxation agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report income specifically exempt under the Income Tax Act, including exempt dividends from South African resident companies, qualifying foreign dividends and certain amounts received by public benefit organisations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The visa advisory business rarely produces exempt income. Non-residents should not claim exemptions on fees from South African clients unless the income is not South African-source or is exempt under a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade expenses incurred in the production of income, including salaries and commissions, premises rentals, advertising, insurance, banking costs, SARS eFiling fees, regulatory licences, travel expenses, professional indemnity premiums, legal costs and depreciation/wear-and-tear allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses actually connected to the production of South African-source income. Cross-border management fees, head-office charges and IT costs must satisfy the arm's-length rule, be supported by written agreements and not merely shift profit offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Assessed loss brought forward and set-off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the unutilised assessed loss from the previous year after applying the set-off rules in section 20 and the section 20A restriction triggered by substantial changes in shareholding or trade continuity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident permanent establishment may utilise assessed losses only to the extent the loss arose from activities attributable to the South African permanent establishment. Losses cannot be imported from the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after deductions and capital gains (inclusion of the Eighth Schedule taxable capital gain), apply the 27% rate, then subtract provisional tax payments, PAYE credits, foreign tax credits, the section 6quat rebate and any other available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident permanent establishment is taxed at the same corporate rate; foreign tax credits may be claimed only if the same income is subject to tax in South Africa and the foreign jurisdiction and the DTA allows relief. Attach a TRC to support treaty credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose cross-border transactions with connected persons, including management fees, royalties, commissions, loans, escrow arrangements and agency relationships. State the country of the connected person and the aggregate value of affected transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must ensure all connected-party dealings are on arm's-length terms. SARS may raise transfer-pricing adjustments under section 31 where the disclosed margins or fees are inconsistent with functions, assets and risks.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file ITR14 by the due date attracts the SARS administrative non-compliance penalty, generally R250 to R10,000 per month based on the company's turnover, capped at a maximum period of 35 months. SARS may also assess interest on underpaid tax, impose understatement penalties up to 200% under section 223, and pursue criminal prosecution for intentional non-compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 Provisional Tax Return; filed electronically through the SARS eFiling portal by all companies unless expressly exempted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual for each year of assessment, with an optional voluntary third top-up payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional estimate and payment due within six months after the start of the year of assessment; second provisional estimate and payment due on or before the last business day of the year of assessment; optional third top-up estimate due within six months after the year-end, in practice aligned with the ITR14 filing process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the reasonable estimate of taxable income for the full year of assessment, using the most recent financial information, adjusted for expected business changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a permanent establishment, the estimate must be limited to South African-source taxable income attributable to the branch, not global group profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% corporate rate, add the inclusion of taxable capital gains, deduct estimated tax credits and any previously paid provisional tax, and arrive at the instalment payable with SARS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty credits only where the same income is taxed abroad and the DTA provides a credit. Attach a concise supporting schedule in a memorandum form for SARS inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Prior period comparison and penalty warning
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compare the current estimate with the prior year taxable income and disclose any material reduction, for example due to COVID-19, discontinued business lines or sudden loss of immigration mandates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch should retain the foreign head-office approval minutes and budgets to substantiate the estimate if SARS challenges an unexpectedly low provisional payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or insufficient provisional payments attract interest at the prescribed rate plus a percentage-based underprovision penalty under the Fourth Schedule and the Tax Administration Act. SARS may also apply the administrative non-compliance penalty for failure to submit the IRP6, and understatement penalties of up to 200% if the estimate is deliberately understated.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividend withholding tax under sections 64E to 64N of the Income Tax Act. The tax is imposed on the gross dividend paid by a South African resident company to a non-resident beneficial owner, subject to exemptions in section 64F and any reduced DTA rate. The company, as the withholding agent, remains liable to account to SARS unless a valid declaration and undertaking are held.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the paying company or regulated intermediary with a completed dividend tax declaration and undertaking containing the beneficial owner's name, address, country of residence, valid tax residence certificate issued by the foreign revenue authority, the relevant DTA article, the percentage shareholding, confirmation that the owner is not acting as a nominee or agent, and confirmation that no permanent establishment in South Africa is effectively connected to the dividend. The declaration must be received before the dividend is paid. If tax is over-withheld, a refund application may be made to SARS under section 64M with the TRC and supporting DTA analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates are 15% for interest paid to non-residents under sections 50A to 50H and 15% for royalties paid to non-residents under sections 49A to 49H. DTA rates vary by convention; many South African treaties reduce interest to 0% or 10% for bank and business interest and reduce royalties to 5% or 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits clauses. For the study-abroad and immigration business, payments labelled as software licensing, business-format fees, visa-processing platform fees, or know-how royalties must be assessed against the royalty definition and supported by economically substantive contracts.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: South African transfer-pricing documentation is generally required for cross-border affected transactions between connected persons where the aggregate value of affected transactions in a year exceeds R5 million. Contemporaneous Local File documentation must evidence comparability, functions, assets and risks, and arm's-length pricing. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational enterprise groups with consolidated group revenue of R10 billion or more in the preceding year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Any other method explicitly accepted as the best transfer-pricing method under section 31 and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines if it yields the most reliable arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not apply a separate Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulation filing. However, the tax system enforces substantive commercial activity through the residence test (place of effective management), the controlled-foreign-company rules in section 9D, the transfer-pricing rules in section 31, the general anti-avoidance rules in sections 80A to 80L, and the common-law doctrines of sham and substance over form. A company holding client fees, escrow accounts or visa-processing contracts but lacking premises, employees, business records, director decisions and commercial risk-taking is vulnerable to being recharacterised, reassessed or disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting cash consulting fees, underreporting student placement commissions, creating false reimbursement claims for visa expenses, channelling corporate income through personal bank accounts, backdating fee invoices, or suppressing escrow receipts in the SARS ITR14.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Tax Administration Act for tax evasion and false statements, with a fine of up to R2 million per offence and imprisonment of up to five years. SARS may also impose an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the shortfall under section 223, plus interest and seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or instruct the evasion are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, civil restitution orders, director disqualification, bank account freezes, seizure of personal assets and travel bans preventing departure from South Africa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee-director South African proprietary limited company with no office, no employees and no real decision-making as a pass-through invoicing vehicle for foreign entities extracting visa and immigration fees, with funds immediately swept to an offshore parent and no board meetings or commercial contracting in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the arrangement under the substance-over-form doctrine or section 80A GAAR, reattribute the income to the true economic owner, impose transfer-pricing adjustments, deny deductions, and apply a 200% understatement penalty if the arrangement is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell company are jointly and severally liable for the company's taxable debts under the Companies Act where reckless trading, fraud or sham conduct is proven; directors may be disqualified and non-resident directors may face cross-border enforcement and visa restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Dividend, Interest or Royalty Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends to non-resident shareholders, paying offshore parent royalties for use of the 'study-abroad' brand, or paying interest to a connected foreign lender without withholding and remitting the applicable 20% dividend or 15% interest/royalty withholding tax to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may assess the unpaid withholding tax together with interest, a late-payment penalty, and an understatement penalty of up to 200%. Criminal prosecution may follow where the failure is deliberate or grossly negligent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for withholding taxes that the company collected or should have collected and failed to pay over to SARS; the Tax Administration Act permits SARS to pursue directors who are or should have been aware of the company's non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, brand royalties, visa-platform software charges or loan interest to a foreign connected party without a written contract, without comparability analysis, without available employees or assets in the foreign entity, or with circular loan structures designed to strip taxable profit out of South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the consideration to an arm's-length price under section 31, denies the deduction for the excess, recharacterises the transaction, imposes interest and understatement penalties up to 200%, and may attribute the profit to a permanent establishment of the foreign entity in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer-pricing declarations face criminal liability; foreign group directors can be assessed as having a permanent establishment in South Africa, and South African directors can be held personally liable for knowing participation in the artificial profit shift.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unlicensed or non-segregated escrow account for client tuition deposits, commingling client funds with operating funds, refusing to identify beneficial owners, failing to maintain FICA records, providing immigration advice fraudulently, or knowingly processing funds derived from a 'guaranteed visa' scam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act imposes administrative fines and criminal penalties for failure to register as an accountable institution, failure to report unusual transactions, and money-laundering complicity. The Prevention of Organised Crime Act allows asset forfeiture and custodial sentences for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in money-laundering or client-fund misappropriation are personally liable for restitution, can be criminally prosecuted, are subject to travel bans and extradition, and may be prohibited from managing any company in South Africa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Exchange Control and Cross-Border Repatriation Abuses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving tuition and visa deposits in foreign currency through unauthorised offshore intermediary accounts, transferring funds from South Africa without South African Reserve Bank approval, using crypto-mixing to avoid exchange-control scrutiny, or mislabelling client escrow repayments as 'consulting fees' to bypass SARB limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contraventions of the Currency and Exchanges Act and SARB Exchange Control Regulations may result in monetary penalties up to the total value involved, confiscation of the funds, revocation of authorised dealer facilities, and criminal sanctions against the entity and responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable to restore unlawfully exported funds; personal assets may be preserved by court order, travel restrictions may be imposed, and non-resident directors may be declared persona non grata by SARS and SARB.
